[BugFix] Require the recompute scheduler only for o_proj/MLP TP (#17436)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Follow-up to #17361: scope the recompute-scheduler requirement it
extended to all four `finegrained_tp_config` knobs back to the two that
need it (`oproj` / `mlp`).

- The requirement exists to keep decode-node steps decode-shaped — a
uniform-token (o_proj/MLP) concern: their exchanges bind the collectives
to the actual per-step token count.
- The lmhead/embedding exchanges are capacity-based — the embedding
exchange pads every step to a deployment-wide capacity constant before
`all_gather` / `reduce_scatter` and trims after, so the collective
shapes are step-count-independent and cannot desync in eager or mixed
steps either.
- lmhead was never gated before #17361; the extension rejects the
bare-`lmhead_tensor_parallel_size` nightly/weekly recipes (no
`recompute_scheduler_enable`) at config load. embedding's coupling
predates the visible repo history with no recorded mechanism basis.
- On the PD MRV2 test bed, `embedding=2` without the recompute scheduler
is bit-identical to the no-knob no-recompute run — no
fine-grained-TP-specific effect. That path has a pre-existing output
defect that reproduces with every knob off (tracked separately), so
gating embedding does not guard it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes: `lmhead_tensor_parallel_size` and `embedding_tensor_parallel_size`
no longer require `recompute_scheduler_enable=true` (restores lmhead to
its pre-#17361 status); `oproj` / `mlp` keep the requirement.

### How was this patch tested?

The bare-lmhead recipes referenced above pass config load again; the
requirement line stays covered by the existing o_proj cases (one test
fixture line added by #17361 is reverted to main's version). CI:
`pre-commit` and `cpu-ut`.

[BugFix] Reshape bf16 wo_a to 3D layout for ModelSlim-quantized DSV4 (#17483)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DSV4 `wo_a` weights must be loaded in the 3D layout`[n_local_groups,
hidden_size, o_lora_rank]` for `npu_transpose_batchmatmul`. The bf16
reshape path introduced by PR #13716 required `quant_config is None`, so
partially-quantized checkpoints (e.g. ModelSlim) that keep FLOAT `wo_a`
alongside a global quant config skipped the reshape. The 2D weight then
crashed the A5 forward (`IndexError` in `npu_transpose_batchmatmul`
`perm_x2`) during ACL graph capture.

Drop the `quant_config is None` condition and judge by dtype only: bf16
`wo_a` is never quantized and has no `process_weights_after_loading`
fallback, so it must be reshaped at load time regardless of the global
quant config. fp8/int8 `wo_a` still resolves False here and is handled
by the quantization path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

no

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit test: `tests/ut/ops/test_linear.py::TestShouldReshapeWoATo3d`
(new regression test covering: bf16 `wo_a` with a global quant config,
non-A5 bf16 `wo_a`, fp8 `wo_a`, and non-`wo_a` layers)
- Manual testing on Ascend A5 (Ascend950) with ModelSlim-quantized
DeepSeek-V4: service starts without crash; `wo_a.weight` shape is 3D
`[n_local_groups, hidden_size, o_lora_rank]`; dummy run passes
- CI for the rest

[BugFix] Fix GLM C8 Config issue (#17448)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fixes the GLM c8 issue: the SFA sparse KV cache dtype was wrongly
resolved from `attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype` (the indexer's own
cache dtype), which is unrelated to the KV cache dtype the user actually
configured.

This PR makes the SFA c8 KV cache dtype follow
`cache_config.cache_dtype` (via `kv_cache_dtype_str_to_dtype`),
consistent with the upstream change in vLLM main commit
`ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607`:

- `vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py`: drop the
`enable_sparse_li_c8`-based dtype resolution and derive `c8_cache_dtype`
from `cache_config.cache_dtype` when `enable_sparse_sfa_c8` is enabled;
use it as `dst_type` for the KV repack op.
- `vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py`: compute `c8_cache_dtype` from
`cache_config.cache_dtype` for the SFA c8 path and use it in
`_reshape_kv_cache_tensors` and `get_kv_cache_spec`.
- `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/attn_utils.py`: apply the same fix in the v2
`get_kv_cache_spec` so the SFA c8 KV cache spec gets the user-configured
dtype.

As a result, the KVCacheSpec dtype now matches the actually allocated KV
cache, and GLM models with a float8 KV cache (e.g. `--kv-cache-dtype
float8_e4m3fn` / `int8`) no longer hit cache dtype mismatch / wrong
cache dtype on the sparse SFA c8 path.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

  No. Bug fix only; no new options or config changes.

[BugFix][310P] Restore hybrid KV cache capacity by sharing Mamba group slots (#17416)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
vLLM 0.29.0 changed hybrid KV cache descriptors from cross-group shared
slots to per-group layer lists. The 310P runners continued to allocate
cache storage per layer, losing the Mamba storage sharing used in
v0.28.0. The worker then reduced the planner budget by 1/4. In the
reported Qwen3.6-27B configuration, reported capacity fell from 166,697
to 41,436 tokens.
This PR:
- Reuses ND Mamba storage for compatible layers at the same position in
different cache groups, in both MRV1 and MRV2.
- Keeps separate NZ K/V storage for each Attention layer and separate
storage for different layers within one group.
- Applies the same sharing eligibility check to allocation and worker
budget calculation, avoiding the extra 1/4 reduction when sharing is
enabled.
- Falls back to the existing per-layer allocation and budget scaling for
unsupported layouts.

[BugFix][Sleep] Keep a dedicated 1 MiB HCCL lifecycle anchor (#15340)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`rl_config.sleep_mode_extra_cleanup` destroys HCCL process groups during
sleep so EP/MC2 windows can be returned to the trainer. Destroying every
multi-rank communicator can tear down shared CANN HCCP/AICPU state.
After restore, the first DSA metadata op (`SparseAttnSharedkvMetadata`)
then fails and `wake_up` returns 500.

This PR does not keep a business group (TP/DP/EP/world). Before teardown
it creates a dedicated world-size HCCL group named
`sleep_lifecycle_anchor` with a **1 MiB** buffer, initializes it with a
device `barrier`, and uses that group as a temporary lifecycle nail:

1. Sleep creates the coordinator on the first cycle, or `restore_hccl()`
on later cycles if the communicator was released after the previous
wake-up.
2. A device barrier physically initializes the nail (HCCL `new_group`
can be lazy).
3. All other HCCL groups are destroyed. If the nail cannot be
established, teardown is skipped for that cycle.
4. Wake-up restores business groups and refreshes MoE/MC2 metadata. The
nail stays up through ACL Graph recapture.
5. After recapture (or after the `kv_cache` stage of level-2 wake-up),
all ranks barrier on the nail and `destroy_hccl()` it. The Python
coordinator is kept (`device_group=None`) and reused next sleep, so the
same group name is not registered twice.

`get_hccl_config_for_pg_options` returns the 1 MiB size for
`sleep_lifecycle_anchor` **before** building the normal config map, so
sleep-time creation does not call `calculate_dp_buffer_size()` /
`get_current_vllm_config()`.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Extra-cleanup creates one temporary 1 MiB world-size HCCL group for
each sleep/wake cycle and releases it after graph recapture. There is no
new environment variable or `rl_config` key.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit tests in `tests/ut/device_allocator/test_sleep_mem_optimized.py`:
  - first-cycle create + reuse / restore of the existing coordinator
  - destroy/restore business groups while skipping the nail
  - skip all HCCL teardown when nail init fails
- release after recapture; keep the nail across staged
`tags=["weights"]` wake-up

[Feature][KV offload] Add fused lightning indexer manage and fused scatter copy sparse flash attention operators for sparse KV cache offloading. (#16640)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds two standalone AscendC custom operators for large-sequence
sparse
KV cache offloading scenarios:

- `fused_lightning_indexer_manage`
- `fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention`

Together, the two operators cover the operator-level workflow from
Lightning
Indexer TopK selection and sparse-cache management to missing-KV scatter
copy
and sparse flash attention.

#### `fused_lightning_indexer_manage`

This operator performs the following operations in a single NPU
invocation:

- Lightning Indexer TopK retrieval;
- initialization and steady-state eviction of the HBM sparse KV cache;
- TopK union management for multiple MTP query routes;
- cache-hit and cache-miss classification;
- generation of cache-miss source IDs and destination HBM slots.

A single batch may contain mixed request states:

- non-offload requests (`request_state = -3`);
- first-offload requests (`request_state = -2`);
- steady-state offload requests (`request_state = -1`).

Each request supports 1 to 14 query routes. The operator maintains the
persistent mapping from source token IDs to HBM logical slots through
`cache_slots_pool`.

The current implementation supports:

- FLOAT16 and BFLOAT16;
- 32 and 64 index heads;
- a fixed index head dimension of 128;
- a fixed TopK size of 2048;
- a cache block size of 128;
- source capacity up to `2^21`;
- Atlas A2 and Atlas A3 products.

`query_dequant_scale` and `index_key_dequant_scale` are reserved inputs
in the
current implementation and are not consumed yet. Quantized Query and
Index Key
dequantization will be supported in a follow-up change.

#### `fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention`

This operator combines missing-KV scatter copy and causal sparse flash
attention in a single public PyTorch custom-op call. It performs the
following
operations:

- initialize the HBM sparse KV cache for first-fill requests;
- identify source-aware TopK cache misses during steady-state execution;
- scatter-copy missing KPE and CKV entries from DRAM to HBM;
- execute causal sparse flash attention over the requested TopK KV
entries;
- support variable numbers of MTP query routes in the TND layout.

A single batch may contain:

- first-fill requests;
- steady-state requests containing cache hits and misses;
- requests with heterogeneous MTP query counts.

Each request supports 1 to 16 query routes, corresponding to MTP0
through
MTP15. The operator consumes the TopK slot and miss metadata produced by
the
cache-management stage.

The current implementation supports:

- FLOAT16 and BFLOAT16;
- 8, 16, 32, 64 and 128 query heads;
- a fixed TopK size of 2048;
- a cache block size of 128;
- a 512-dimensional compressed KV representation;
- a 64-dimensional RoPE key representation;
- Atlas A2 and Atlas A3 products.

The operator uses two execution paths selected from device-side
metadata:

- first-fill path: an internal helper fills the HBM sparse cache before
the
  attention kernel accesses it;
- steady-state path: missing KV entries are copied while sparse
attention is
  executed.

The first-fill helper and the main fused kernel are launched on the same
NPU
stream. The helper becomes a device-side no-op for steady-state
requests. Path
selection does not read CPU data and supports ACLGraph Capture and
Replay.

#### Main changes

- add the two fused AscendC operator implementations;
- add the conditional first-fill scatter-copy helper;
- add operator definitions, tiling implementations and inference
functions;
- add shape, dtype, device, contiguity and dynamic-input validation;
- add ACLNN interfaces and PyTorch custom-op registration;
- add Meta implementations;
- enable the operators for Atlas A2 and Atlas A3 products;
- add operator documentation and representative latency results;
- add standalone correctness and ACLGraph replay tests.

This PR only introduces the standalone operators and their
operator-level
tests. Framework-side metadata construction, cache-manager integration
and
model execution integration are not included and will be submitted
separately.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

Two new PyTorch custom operators are exposed:

```python
torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_fused_lightning_indexer_manage(...)
torch.ops._C_ascend.npu_fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention(...)
```

No existing API, model execution path or default behavior is changed.
The new
operators are not connected to the vLLM model execution path in this PR.

### How was this patch tested?

The operators were built and tested on an Ascend NPU environment.

Test environment:

- Device: Ascend 910_93
- CANN: 9.1.0
- npu-smi: 25.2.1
- OS: Linux
- Python: 3.12.13
- pytest: 8.3.2
- vLLM: `0.1.dev21135+g84030bbe3`

#### Lightning Indexer and cache-management tests

Test command:

```bash
pytest -sv \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_fused_lightning_indexer_manage.py
```

Test result:

```text
collected 105 items
105 passed, 14 warnings in 27.91s
```

The tests use `torch_npu.npu_lightning_indexer` as the TopK reference
implementation and cover:

- FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 and 32/64 index heads;
- all query route counts from Q1 to Q14;
- non-offload, first-offload and steady-state requests;
- mixed request states and lifecycle transitions;
- cache initialization, eviction, hit/miss classification and miss
union;
- repeated invocation and all-hit convergence;
- miss-occurrence boundaries around 2048 and 4096;
- long source IDs from `2^17` to near the `2^21` upper limit;
- representative invalid shape, dtype, contiguity and query-count
inputs.

All 105 correctness cases passed, including the Q14 state matrix,
mixed-state
batch cases and long-sequence cases.

#### Scatter-copy sparse flash attention tests

Test command:

```bash
pytest -sv \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention.py
```

The tests cover:

- FLOAT16/BFLOAT16 and 8/16/32/64/128 query heads;
- MTP0 and heterogeneous MTP2/MTP3/MTP8/MTP15 TND batches;
- steady-state fused scatter copy;
- first-fill requests and mixed-request batches;
- `attention_out` precision against a CPU reference;
- HBM KPE and CKV cache update correctness;
- ACLGraph Capture and Replay;
- switching from the captured steady-state path to the first-fill path
through
  device-side metadata.

Representative latency results for both operators are included in their
respective README files. They are provided as reference data only and
are not
used as test thresholds.

### End-to-end inference results

The operators were also evaluated end-to-end with GLM-5.2-w4a8 on Ascend
910C,
using TP16/EP16 and a 64K sequence length.

With the same batch size of 5, enabling KV cache offloading increases
ITL only
from 73.56 ms to 78.42 ms, corresponding to a 6.6% degradation.

With KV cache offloading enabled, the batch size can be increased from 5
to 16.
In this configuration, ITL increases from 73.56 ms to 109.54 ms, while
throughput increases from 188 TPS to 406 TPS, corresponding to a 115%
throughput improvement.

The operator-level contributions are as follows:

* `fused_lightning_indexer_manage`: at batch size 5 without offloading,
the
  total latency of the Lightning Indexer operators across all layers is
  2.89 ms. At batch size 5 with offloading, the total latency of the LIM
  operators across all layers is 6.83 ms, resulting in only a 3.94 ms
  increase in ITL.

* `fused_scatter_copy_sparse_flash_attention`: at batch size 16, with
separate
scatter-copy and sparse flash attention operators, the total
scatter-copy
latency across all layers is 11.75 ms and the total sparse flash
attention
latency is 18.81 ms. With the fused CopySFA operator, the total latency
across all layers is 23.90 ms. Therefore, the fused operator reduces ITL
by
  `11.75 + 18.81 - 23.90 = 6.66 ms`.

Compared with the first version of the fused operators, evaluated with 4
machines, 1P1D, 32 concurrent requests and a 29K sequence length, ITL is
reduced from 80 ms in the first version

([https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14278](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/14278))
to 77.7 ms with the
current implementation, corresponding to a 2.3 ms ITL reduction. There
is
still room for further optimization on the framework side.

[BugFix] Solve the d2h free_bubble in glm5.2 dspark (#17184)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
In the scenario where GLM5.2 enables dspark, the seq_lens in
attention_v1 requires a device-to-host synchronization (on the NPU,
seq_lens has num_rejects subtracted, whereas on the CPU it does not),
causing a large number of bubbles between the main model and the draft
model. Since seq_lens is a device tensor, performing a tolist()
operation triggers a device-to-host synchronization. Therefore, a
whitelist approach is used to address this scenario. Empirical tests
show that using seq_lens without num_rejects has almost no impact on the
model acceptance rate, but greatly improves performance.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
no

[Feature][SpecDecode] Enable ACL graph mode for GLM-Next MTP draft models (#17178)

### What this PR does / why we need it

GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`, draft model `glm5_next_mtp`) uses MTP
speculative decoding with draft layers split across multiple physical
KV-cache groups:

- primary MLA attention
- indexer KPool
- compressor tail

The generic GLM speculative-decoding path previously forced the draft
model to run eagerly. In addition, the multi-KV-group runtime metadata
was rebuilt using per-round tensor clones. Although correct in eager
mode, these dynamically allocated tensors are incompatible with ACL
graph replay, which requires the captured input addresses to remain
stable.

This PR enables ACL graph mode for the specialized
`AscendMultiKVCacheGroupMTPProposer` used by `glm5_next_mtp`.

Other GLM speculative-decoding implementations remain forced to eager
mode. Users can still explicitly keep the GLM-Next MTP draft eager by
setting `"enforce_eager": true` in the speculative configuration.

The main changes are:

1. **GLM-Next MTP graph capability**

The specialized multi-KV-group proposer declares support for GLM draft
graph mode. The generic GLM forced-eager behavior remains unchanged for
other GLM draft implementations.

2. **Graph-stable common metadata**

Persistent per-`(KV-cache group, draft step)` slot-mapping buffers
replace per-round clones. Capture and runtime drafting therefore reuse
the same tensor addresses.

3. **Graph-stable KPool derived metadata**

   `AscendIndexerKPoolMetadataBuilder` keeps persistent buffers for:

   - compressed slot mappings
   - sequence lengths
   - cumulative query lengths
   - raw sequence lengths
   - positions

The buffers are keyed by the persistent common slot-mapping address so
that capture and replay bind the same storage.

4. **FULL graph padding support**

   Request-shaped KPool metadata buffers are sized using:

   ```python
   max(max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens)
   ```

This covers FULL draft graph padding, where the padded request dimension
may exceed `max_num_seqs`. For example, four requests with MTP K=3 use a
16-token graph bucket.

5. **Cache-only builder graph entrypoints**

`build_for_graph_capture` and `build_for_drafting` are implemented for
the KPool and KPool-tail cache-only metadata builders.

6. **Multi-group graph-capture routing**

Graph capture builds a separate metadata view for each physical KV-cache
group and routes executable and cache-only groups through their
appropriate metadata-builder entrypoints.

7. **FULL-mode sequence-length robustness**

`seq_lens_cpu` may be intentionally invalidated during the first MTP
draft transition to avoid a device-to-host synchronization. The
FULL-mode updater now handles the field being `None`, consistently with
the existing guards for `_seq_lens_cpu` and `num_computed_tokens_cpu`.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes.

When ACL graph mode is enabled for the target model, `glm5_next_mtp`
drafting now uses ACL graph mode by default. Other GLM speculative draft
implementations remain eager.

Users can explicitly disable draft graph mode with:

```json
{
  "method": "mtp",
  "num_speculative_tokens": 3,
  "enforce_eager": true
}
```

The first request using a previously uncaptured draft bucket may incur a
one-time lazy graph-capture cost of approximately 10–15 seconds.
Subsequent replays use the captured graph.

### How was this patch tested?

#### Unit tests

Extended:

- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_multi_kv_cache_group_proposer.py`
- `tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kv_cache.py`

The tests cover:

- persistent address semantics across metadata rebuilds
- independent buffers for different MTP draft steps
- KPool graph-capture and drafting entrypoints
- FULL-mode operation with absent CPU sequence lengths
- padded `num_reqs` exceeding `max_num_seqs`
- multi-group graph-capture metadata routing

The targeted unit-test suites pass with 40+ test cases.

#### End-to-end validation

Hardware and configuration:

- Atlas A3, 8 × Ascend 910
- tensor parallel size 8
- expert parallel enabled
- GLM-5.3-Flash W8A8
- MTP K=3
- target graph mode: `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`
- graph capture sizes up to 128

Results:

- draft buckets 4, 8, 16 and 32 passed
- request concurrency 1, 2, 4 and 8 passed
- all requests returned coherent output
- rejection-sampler acceptance remained 75%–100%
- greedy graph-mode output was bit-exact with the eager baseline across
  20 `(prompt, concurrency)` pairs
- repeated graph batches produced identical output, with no
stale-metadata
  regression

Steady-state latency at concurrency 4 improved from 1.028 s to 0.863 s
(approximately 1.19×).

At concurrency 8, graph mode also reduced latency. The measured mean was
1.984 s to 1.073 s, although the eager sample contained several
approximately 5-second outliers; the corresponding median changed from
approximately 1.25 s to 1.10 s.

### Notes

The remaining family-wide GLM forced-eager path is intentionally
retained for GLM draft implementations that have not declared graph
support.

[BugFix] Fix `UpdatableGraph` curl error in `PCP` by rebuilding draft block table (#17240)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
**Bug**
In the PCP scenario, `UpdatableGraph` causes curl to fail with an error.

**Root Cause**
In PCP, the draft model cannot use the same `block_table` as the main
model. Without rebuilding it, the draft model gets an incorrect
`block_table`, which leads to the curl error.

**Solution**
- Extract `build_draft_attn_metadatas` into a shared path for both code
paths, since the pre-refactor path already used it.
- Obtain the rebuilt `block_table` and pass it to the graph for
parameter updates.
### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No.
### How was this patch tested?
Manually A/B tested.

[feature] Speed up startup for DeepSeek V4 (#16548)

Fixes #16552

Large-EP PD serving (Flash, Pro, GLM, and similar). Startup used to scan
the full quant description once per RMSNorm, JIT 16 RMS BLOCK_M values,
and pay the first NZ format-cast plus Triton compile only after weight
I/O.

## **1. Background**

Same Flash-best startup changes as the 0.26 PR, ported to the main
package layout. is_layer_skipped_ascend is already O(1) on main
(#16051), so that index is not in this PR. Main already treats a missing
quant_description[prefix + ".weight"] as unquantized, so the 0.26 Pro
MTP mtp.0.head.weight KeyError does not apply here.

The old CPU-then-NPU expert path is dropped. It failed Prefill dummy_run
with Expected NPU tensor. The hash-router id2eid table stays as it is on
main.

## **2. Design**

Two opt-in prewarm threads live under
dditional_config.ascend_warmup_config. Both default to false (review
feedback from @yiz-liu and @kunpengW-code):

- enable_early_nz_warmup: pays the first NZ format-cast lazy init during
weight I/O. This is independent of the quantization scheme, so it lives
in model_executor/warmup/nz_warmup.py with the other startup warmups.
- enable_early_kernel_warmup: compiles the Triton warmup kernels during
weight I/O.

`json
"additional_config": {
    "ascend_warmup_config": {
        "enable_early_kernel_warmup": true,
        "enable_early_nz_warmup": true
    }
}
`

NPUModelRunner.load_model starts both threads before get_model() and
joins them before it returns. Every model can use them, and both threads
finish before memory profiling and KV cache allocation.

The MTP embed-table skip from the 0.26 PR is not included. DeepSeek V4
always has compress_ratios, so that branch never ran (review feedback
from @Angazenn).

No loader default is changed. A netloader disk fallback used to drop the
whole model_loader_extra_config and silently disable the user's
multithread load. It now keeps the keys DefaultModelLoader accepts and
drops only the netloader-only keys. Thread-count defaults stay with vLLM
(review feedback from @nu11ptr7).

[BugFix][KV Pool] Fix layerwise cache group indexing under PP (#17246)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

With layerwise AscendStore and multiple KV cache groups, a nonzero PP
stage can raise `IndexError` in
`LayerBatchBuilder._build_transfer_arrays()` when indexing
`_layer_cache_entry_offsets_np`. The group map has used stage-local
layer IDs since #16412, but #16208 added the global PP offset when
looking up save/load tasks. A missed lookup falls back to group 0 with a
stage-local index that can exceed that group's layer count or select the
wrong cache address.

Use stage-local IDs in the GVA branch of
`_groups_for_layerwise_transfer()`, which now serves both save and load
on main. Pool key and remote-address offsets remain unchanged. Extend
the existing PP regression test through real save/load task and address
construction for both PP stages, checking the local layer/task counts
and expected tensor addresses.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes incorrect group selection and layer-index errors in layerwise PP
deployments with multiple cache groups, including the reported DSv4 +
Memcache scenario. No configuration changes.

[Performance][DSV4] Reuse filtered RoPE lookups (#17067)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR removes redundant DeepSeek V4 RoPE table indexing that remains
on current main.

- adds an optional layer filter to `get_cos_and_sin_dsa` so draft
attention queries only the RoPE config consumed by its layers
- resolves draft `*.swa_cache` layer names to their registered `*.attn`
RoPE layer
- computes the ordinary RoPE cos/sin pair once before the DSpark
context-KV layer loop and reuses it across all draft layers
- preserves existing target common/decode caching already present on
current main

Current main has already absorbed part of the older optimization design,
so this PR deliberately excludes that existing logic. It is independent
of the block-table dirty-copy PR.

An earlier DSV4 DP16 decode profile showed that eliminating 26 redundant
Index/IndexCheck pairs saved approximately 1.19 ms/step. On current
main, only the draft config filtering and cross-layer context-KV reuse
remain applicable, so a fresh profile is required before making a
current-main performance claim.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or output change. RoPE values are queried for the same positions
and config; the result is reused by layers that share that config.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added unit coverage verifying layer-based config filtering and
`swa_cache` to `attn` resolution.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed: Ruff check/format, codespell,
typos, gitleaks, import and policy checks, and DCO sign-off.
- `python3 -m compileall` and `git diff --check` passed for the changed
files.

NPU execution was not run locally. Required follow-up coverage on Ascend
is: DSV4/DSpark eager correctness, affected attention backend smoke with
real weights, graph-mode coverage, and a fresh Index/IndexCheck profile.
